words_to_read_new.meaning: e- means out of + RUPT means break: to break out, like lava from a volcano
e- means out of + RUPT means break + -ion means the act of: the act of breaking out
inter- means between + RUPT means break: to break in between, to cut in while someone talks
inter- means between + RUPT means break + -ion means the act of: the act of breaking in
RUPT means break + -ure means the result of: a break or burst, like a burst pipe
ab- means away + RUPT means break: broken off, so sudden
bank + RUPT means break: a broken bank, not able to pay what you owe
bank + RUPT means break + -cy means state: the state of being bankrupt
dis- means apart + RUPT means break: to break apart, to throw into a mess

associated_word_exceptions.reason: Ground 3: the -cy card lists bankruptcy; bankrupt is its simpler sibling (bank + rupt, nothing untaught), and the financial maths unit running this term needs it.
associated_word_exceptions.source: Macquarie Dictionary: bankrupt, a person who is unable to pay their debts; from Italian banca rotta, broken bench.

associated_word_exceptions.reason: Ground 2: printed on the taught -cy suffix card's associated words; it stacks rupt with the taught -cy.

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
SAY: "Learn rupt once and you can read a whole family of words about breaking."
READ each word as it appears, say what it means, then link rupt to the card meaning: break.
erupt - e means out of + RUPT means break: to break out. The volcano began to erupt.
eruption - e + RUPT + ion means the act of: the act of breaking out. The eruption sent ash into the sky.
interrupt - inter means between + RUPT: to break in between. Please do not interrupt the speaker.
interruption - inter + RUPT + ion: the act of breaking in. A fire drill was an interruption to our test.
rupture - RUPT + ure means the result of: a break or burst. A rupture in the pipe flooded the street.
abrupt - ab means away + RUPT: broken off, so sudden. The bus came to an abrupt stop.
bankrupt - bank + RUPT: a broken bank. A business that cannot pay what it owes is bankrupt.
bankruptcy - bank + RUPT + cy means state: the state of being bankrupt. The shop closed after its bankruptcy.
disrupt - dis means apart + RUPT: to break apart, to throw into a mess. Loud talking can disrupt a lesson.

keyword_sentence.title: Pick your own rupt word
keyword_sentence.rule: Two jobs in your OG book
keyword_sentence.example:
1. Your own rupt word for break. Star it.
2. Write one sentence that shows what it means.
items: My word: **erupt** - The volcano began to **erupt** with lava.
keyword_sentence.footer: Check: does it make the meaning clear?
keyword_sentence.notes:
1. SAY: "The card keyword is abrupt. Ab means away, rupt means break: broken off, so sudden. The music stopped with an abrupt crash."
2. SAY: "If another rupt word helps YOU remember break, pick that one, like erupt. Write it at the bottom of the page and star it."
3. SAY: "Then write one sentence with your word, so a reader can tell what it means." TIME: 3 min, then cold call two students to read theirs.
EXTENSION: Two in one - write one sentence that uses two rupt words and still makes sense.
HELP: give a stem, "The volcano began to..." or "Please do not interrupt...", and let them finish it.
---
ANSWERS: open - e.g. Mine: erupt. The volcano began to erupt with lava. EXTENSION: e.g. The eruption was an abrupt end to our holiday.

matrix.title: Build rupt words
matrix.rule: Build real words. Write each one and what it means.
matrix.notes:
1. SAY: "rupt is in the middle. Join a part from the left, the right, or both, and build a real word. Write the word and what it means."
2. MODEL: say "e plus rupt: erupt, to break out", and write it on the class board.
3. TIME: 4 min. CIRCULATE: to a stuck student say, "Start with rupt. Put inter in front. What does interrupt mean?"
4. ASK: "Read me your longest word and what it means." Cold call two students. EXPECT: interruption, the act of breaking in; eruptive, relating to breaking out.
TRAP: a made-up word that sounds right, like erupture. Fix: ask, would you read that in a newspaper? Student builds a real one.
EXTENSION: Longest word hunt - build the longest real word you can and write its parts.
HELP: give three starters, erupt, interrupt, abrupt, and ask for one ending on each.
---
ANSWERS: erupt, interrupt, abrupt, rupture; add -ion for the act of: eruption, interruption.
Also: eruptive (relating to breaking out); erupted, erupting, interrupted, interrupting, ruptured.
EXTENSION: e.g. interruption = inter + rupt + ion; eruptive = e + rupt + ive.

rounds.title: Break the word into its parts
rounds.rule: Write only the parts in the boxes. rupt is done for you.

round.notes:
1. SAY: "We just built words. Now we do the opposite. I show a whole word, you write its parts in boxes."
2. MODEL: point at erupting. SAY: "I find rupt first. In front is e. Behind is ing. Three parts, three boxes: e, rupt, ing."
3. SAY: "Three words, one at a time. Write only the parts in your OG book, then I click."
EXTENSION: Beat the number - break 5 more rupt words from the matrix into parts in 2 minutes.
HELP: underline rupt in each word first, then split what is left on each side.
---
ANSWERS: 1. ab + rupt + ly  2. rupt + ure + s  3. inter + rupt + ed. EXTENSION: e.g. e + rupt + ion, inter + rupt + ion, e + rupt + ive.

rounds.title: Choose the best meaning
rounds.rule: Which meaning uses every part? Fingers: 1, 2 or 3.
rounds.footer: Check: did you use every part?

round.notes:
1. SAY: "Last round. I show a word and three meanings. Only one uses every part of the word."
2. MODEL: "Erupted. E means out of, rupt means break, ed means it already happened. Broke in has break, but the wrong way. Pulled out has the right way, but pull is tract. Broke out uses every part."
3. SAY: "Three more. Read the word, find each part, then show me one, two or three fingers on three."

round.rule: Use every part: -ion (the act of). Fingers: 1, 2 or 3.
round.notes:
ANSWER: 2 - the act of breaking out.
1. ASK: "Read eruption in your head. Which meaning uses every part? One, two or three fingers, voices off, show me on three." 10 sec.
2. SCAN the fingers. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> point at the e and ask what it means, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after fingers are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. E means out of, rupt means break, ion means the act of. An eruption is the act of breaking out."
TRAP: 1, the act of breaking in. Fix: break is right, but e means out of; student finds the choice with out.

round.rule: Use every part: -ion (the act of). Fingers: 1, 2 or 3.
round.notes:
ANSWER: 3 - the act of breaking in.
1. ASK: "Read interruption in your head. Which meaning uses every part? One, two or three fingers, voices off, show me on three." 10 sec.
2. SCAN the fingers. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> point at inter and ask what it means, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after fingers are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Inter means between, ion means the act of. Breaking in between, like a fire drill in a test."
TRAP: 2, the act of building in. Fix: building is struct, not rupt; student finds the choice with break.

ANSWER: 1 - the state of being broke.
1. ASK: "Read bankruptcy in your head. Which meaning uses every part? One, two or three fingers, voices off, show me on three." 10 sec.
2. SCAN the fingers. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> point at cy and ask what it means, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after fingers are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Cy means state, and a broken bank has no money. Bankruptcy is the state of being broke."
TRAP: 2, one who breaks a bank. Fix: break is right, but cy means state, not one who; student finds the choice with state.
EXTENSION: Make your own - write a rupt word with three parts and three meanings for a partner, one right and one nearly right.
---
ANSWERS: erupted - broke out (worked), eruption 2, interruption 3, bankruptcy 1.

intro.title: Noun, verb or adjective?
intro.rule: Read the sentence. What job does the bold word do?
intro.prompt: Mia gave me **constructive** advice about my speech.
intro.footer: Next: your turn on four suffix cards
intro.notes:
ANSWER: adjective - constructive describes the advice.
1. SAY: "Every word has a job in a sentence. The sentence tells us the job, and the suffix helps."
2. POINT at each choice. SAY: "A noun names a thing or idea. A verb is something you do. An adjective describes a noun."
3. MODEL: read the sentence. SAY: "What sort of advice? Constructive advice. Constructive tells us about the advice."
4. SAY: "The doing word is gave. Advice is the thing. Constructive describes the advice, so it is an adjective." REVEAL on the click.
5. SAY: "Construct is something you do. Add -ive, relating to, and it describes a noun. The suffix changed the job."
TRAP: verb, because construct is an action. Fix: cover the -ive, then show it; student says what the suffix changed.

cards.sentence: The puppy was very playful in its infancy.

SCAN: split or wrong chorus -> do not click. Ask "When was the puppy playful?", then re-ask on three.
3. REVEAL after the choral answer. SAY: "Infancy names a time of life, the state of being a baby, so it is a noun. -cy words name a state, so they are nouns."

grammar.header_notes:
PURPOSE: A simple sentence has one M. A compound sentence has two M joined by a comma and and, but, so, or or yet.
WHY THIS WEEK: persuasive writers join a point and its result with , so and a point and its problem with , but. Students who see two M stop writing run-ons.
TIME: 5 minutes, no more - I do 1 min, We do 1 question, You do 3 questions at about 30 seconds each. One question per slide; your click reveals the answer.
ROUTINE: all grammar is written in the OG book. No boards - books, fingers and voices only. Smackdown signals: one finger simple, two fingers compound, fist leaves you waiting.
CHECK: and between two doing words is not a compound. The volcano rumbled and erupted has one M - nothing on the right stands alone.

i_do.title: Simple or compound?
i_do.rule: One M = simple. Two M joined by and, but or so = compound.
i_do.example:
The volcano rumbled,
so the villagers ran to the boats.
items: Chop at the joining word. Does each side stand alone?
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: compound - The volcano rumbled (M), so (joining word), the villagers ran to the boats (M).
1. SAY: "A simple sentence has one M. When we join two M with a comma and and, but or so, we get a compound sentence."
2. WRITE: copy the sentence on the class board. Hand chop before so. Read "The volcano rumbled". It stands alone, so write M under it.
3. WRITE: read "the villagers ran to the boats". It stands alone too, so write M under it. CIRCLE so and the comma in front of it.
4. ASK: "One M or two? One finger simple, two fingers compound, voices off, show me on three." 5 sec. EXPECT: two fingers.
TRAP: calling any long sentence compound. Fix: chop at the joining word and read each side; if one side cannot stand alone, it is not compound.
CLARIFY: if a student asks about because, say it makes one side wait, so that is the fist - last week's complex sentence.
---
PREP: coordinating conjunctions (and, but, so, or, yet) join two independent clauses; a comma goes before the conjunction.

we_do.title: Simple, compound or complex?
we_do.rule: Chop at the joining word. Does each side stand alone?

round.prompt:
The polar bear sniffed the air
and padded across the ice.
round.why: one M - the bear did two things
round.notes:
ANSWER: simple - one M. The bear did two things, joined by and.
1. SAY: "Read it in your head. Chop at and, then read each side."
2. ASK: "One finger simple, two fingers compound, fist complex, voices off, show me on three." 5 sec. EXPECT: one finger.
3. REVEAL after hands are scanned. ASK: "How do you know?" Cold call one student. EXPECT: padded across the ice cannot stand alone - it has no who.
TRAP: two fingers, because of and. Fix: read padded across the ice on its own; it has no who, student shows one finger.
CLARIFY: if a student asks how to make it compound, say add a who: The polar bear sniffed the air, and it padded across the ice.

you_do.title: Simple or compound?
you_do.rule: Write simple or compound. Circle the joining word if it joins two M.
you_do.footer: Check: chop - does each side stand alone?

round.prompt:
Our brochure was colourful,
but nobody picked it up.
round.notes:
ANSWER: compound - but.
1. SAY: "Write simple or compound. Circle the joining word if it joins two M. Pens down when you are done."
2. TIME: 30 sec. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> chop before but and read each side aloud, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Our brochure was colourful stands alone. Nobody picked it up stands alone. Two M, so compound."
TRAP: simple, because it is about one brochure. Fix: count the M, not the topics; chop and read, student writes compound.
EXTENSION: Two in one - write one compound sentence with a rupt word on each side. Label both M.
HELP: give the joining words - and, but, so - and ask which one is in the sentence, then read each side.

round.prompt:
The old pipe ruptured
and flooded the kitchen.
round.why: one M - the pipe did two things
round.notes:
ANSWER: simple.
1. SAY: "Write simple or compound. Pens down when you are done."
2. TIME: 30 sec. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> read flooded the kitchen on its own and ask who flooded it, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. Flooded the kitchen has no who, so it cannot stand alone. One M: the pipe ruptured and flooded."
TRAP: compound, because of and. Fix: and joins two doing words here; read the right side alone, student writes simple.

round.prompt:
The fire alarm rang,
so it interrupted our speeches.
round.notes:
ANSWER: compound - so.
1. SAY: "Last one. Write simple or compound, and circle the joining word. Pens down when you are done."
2. TIME: 30 sec. SCAN four books near you. 80%+ -> click to reveal. Less -> chop before so and read each side, then re-ask.
3. REVEAL after books are scanned. SAY: "Tick it or fix it. The fire alarm rang stands alone, and it interrupted our speeches stands alone. Two M joined by , so."
4. SAY: "In your persuasive piece, find one place where , so or , but joins two of your points."
TRAP: circling interrupted. Fix: that is the doing word; the joining word sits after the comma, student circles so.
---
ANSWERS: 1. compound - but  2. simple  3. compound - so. EXTENSION: e.g. The volcano began to erupt (M), so the bus came to an abrupt stop (M).

EXPECT: bankruptcy.
4. ASK: "Which word means pulled toward, like a magnet pulls a pin?"
10 sec, turn and talk. Then: "Everyone, together, on three."
EXPECT: attracted.

subblocks.heading: Join two simple sentences
subblocks.instruction: Join the pair into one compound sentence. Use a comma and and, but or so.
example: The bell rang. We packed up.  ->  The bell rang, so we packed up.

items: Our stall had great posters. Nobody bought a thing.

answers: Our stall had great posters, but nobody bought a thing.

subblocks.heading: Make it compound
subblocks.instruction: This sentence is simple: one M. Rewrite it as a compound sentence. Add a comma before and, then a second who.

items: The crowd cheered and clapped for the speaker.

answers: The crowd cheered, and they clapped for the speaker.

part_b.title: Parts of Speech: noun, verb or adjective

subblocks.heading: What job does the word in capitals do?
subblocks.instruction: Read each sentence. Write the job of the word in CAPITALS: noun, verb or adjective.
tip: noun - names a thing or idea. verb - something you do. adjective - describes a noun.
e.g. The PIGLET slept in the straw. PIGLET = noun (the thing that slept).

items: The vet will EXAMINE the puppy's ears.
Our school has a no hat, no play POLICY.
The shop sells GENUINE leather boots.
Gran took a TABLET for her sore throat.
The boats sheltered in a rocky INLET.

answers: examine - what the vet will do - verb
policy - the thing our school has - noun
tablet - the thing Gran took - noun
inlet - the thing the boats sheltered in - noun

subblocks.heading: Complete the sentence
subblocks.instruction: Write the learned word that fits each gap. Spell it carefully.

items: The travel agent's glossy ___ tried to persuade us to visit Fiji.
Our class captain is the ___ between students and teachers.

subblocks.heading: rupt = break
subblocks.instruction: Break each word into its parts, then write what the parts mean. Use the parts box.
example: abruptly = ab + rupt + ly = away + break + in a way that
answers: eruption = e + rupt + ion = out of + break + the act of
interruption = inter + rupt + ion = between + break + the act of
bankruptcy = bank + rupt + cy = bank + break + state

subblocks.heading: rupt = break: new words
subblocks.instruction: These words were not on our lists. Use the parts to work out what each one means.
answers: uninterrupted: not broken in between - it went on with no breaks (like an uninterrupted sleep)
interrupter: one who breaks in between (someone who cuts in while others talk)

dictation.sentence: The volcano began to erupt, so the tourists ran back to the bus.

punctuation: comma before so (it joins two full sentences)

dictation.sentence: Our class liaison handed out a brochure, but the crowd kept interrupting her.
chunks: Our class liaison handed out a brochure,

punctuation: comma before but (it joins two full sentences)

follow_up.question: Part A, Q1
follow_up.flag_when: the comma left out, or the two sentences still split by a full stop
follow_up.next_move: In next week's dictation, read two short sentences and ask the class to join them with , so on whiteboards.

follow_up.question: Part A, Q2
follow_up.flag_when: a comma added but no second who, so the right side cannot stand alone
follow_up.next_move: During Words to Read Review, say "The bear sniffed, and padded away" and ask what the right side needs to stand alone.

follow_up.question: Part B, Q1
follow_up.flag_when: 2 or more of the 5 jobs wrong
follow_up.next_move: Before next week's suffix cards, say: Our class will engineer a raft. The engineer fixed it. Ask what job engineer does each time.

follow_up.question: Part C, Q1
follow_up.next_move: During Words to Spell Review, add "liaison" on the class whiteboard and ask which three vowels sit in a row.

follow_up.question: Part D, Q1
follow_up.flag_when: rupt = break missing, or 2 of the 3 sums wrong
follow_up.next_move: During the review cards, stop on rupt and ask for two rupt words and what each part means.

follow_up.question: Part D, Q2
follow_up.flag_when: a meaning that ignores rupt (break) or the printed part
follow_up.next_move: During Words to Read Review, add "uninterrupted" on the class whiteboard and ask what is not broken.

follow_up.question: Part E
follow_up.flag_when: 3 or more COPS points lost across the two sentences
follow_up.next_move: In next week's dictation, stop after the CHECK step and have the student redo their weakest COPS letter aloud with you.
